meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale, and a client call at 4:40. Owen found out about a zero from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. Who decided that, and why didn't anyone call me first?
Sit down? I'd rather stand. You asked for this meeting, Hale, so tell me what you have. I haven't heard an answer to who decided the zero.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero on Owen's essay be withdrawn and that nothing go on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a written promise that nothing goes on Owen's record.
What moved her: nothing, because "Thanks for coming in." gave her no evidence to weigh.
What cost ground: nothing, though "Thanks for coming in." let her question about who decided the zero and why no one called her go unanswered.
Try next time: when she asks who decided and why no one called, answer that directly, owning the process in one sentence before you put a dated document in front of her.
